DPZ.thesis: High-quality, cash-backed franchisor (F-score 8/9, cfo $792M vs net income $602M, gross profitability 1.15) with a 252d beta of 0.095 (-$0.62 on this position in a 10% market drop). That makes it a genuinely defensive starter position while the tape rotates away from tech. Its top-of-sector rank is partly an artifact of the wholesale-groceries mislabel, so the case rests on its absolute quality and low beta, not on the Staples tilt. No earnings inside 5 trading days.

IDXX.thesis: Quality Health Care name (F-score 8/9, gp_sector_pct 0.942, CFO $1,181.8M vs net income $1,059.5M, no added leverage or dilution). The 11-02 print beat and raised guidance; next earnings 2027-02-01. Health Care is no longer on the Market Analyst's favored list (as of 11-20), so the case rests on quality and the beat-and-raise, not a sector tilt. Its 0.80 beta is the highest of the single stocks, which makes it the least defensive holding in a risk-off book. Executives sold over $27M of stock after the run. It is the next trim candidate: the Proposer owes a trim proposal or an explicit hold verdict at the next run (L8).

TLT.thesis: A small defensive Treasury sleeve while the regime filter allows only BND, GLD, IEF and TLT. The Market Analyst says Treasuries are the better defensive choice and that duration is hedging again (TLT and IEF rose over 5 days while SPY fell). TLT is used because IEF and BND are wash-sale blocked, not because he prefers it; it is the most volatile Treasury option and he calls the move young, so it is sized at $25 (cut from $40) on one week of evidence. It adds long-duration rate risk that the equity stress test does not show, with the 12-09 FOMC inside its 20-session test. TLT tracks 20+ year Treasuries and is judged not substantially identical to the blocked IEF. ETF, no earnings events. No other bond ETF is held.
TLT.invalidation: TLT closes at or below $76.30 (about 5% under the $80.35 reference close of 11-19; to be restated from the actual fill at the next run), or at any run TLT's and IEF's 5-day returns are both negative while SPY's 5-day return is also negative (duration no longer hedging, per the Market Analyst's figures).
